pages.summary: A signal with white Gaussian noise added, at a signal-to-noise ratio.
body: The noise's power is the signal's power divided by the ratio: snr in dB (or `'linear'`), the signal's power in dBW (0, that is 1 W, unless given) or `'measured'` from x itself. A complex signal gets complex noise, half its power in each part. A seed draws the noise from a generator of its own, so that the same call gives the same noise.
syntax: Noise at snr dB, the signal taken as 1 W.
The signal's power given, in dBW.
snr and sigpower as ratios, not dB.

examples.title: A sine at 10 dB, and the ratio measured back

pages.summary: Quadrature amplitude modulation: integers or bits to points in the complex plane, and back.
body: Square M-QAM (M = 2 or a power of 4) places the integers 0 to M-1 on a square grid of odd levels, ±1, ±3, ...: half of each integer's bits pick the in-phase level and half the quadrature level, each Gray coded so that neighbours differ in one bit, unless `symOrder` is `'bin'` or a mapping. `'InputType', 'bit'` takes groups of log2(M) bits, the first the most significant; `'UnitAveragePower'` scales the points to an average power of 1. `qamdemod` gives the nearest point's integer, its bits, or each bit's log-likelihood ratio (`'llr'`, with the noise's variance).
syntax: Bits to points of unit average power.

examples.title: 16-QAM through noise
The constellation's labels
examples.intro: Gray coding: along the top row of 16-QAM, each point's label differs from the next in one bit.

pages.summary: Phase shift keying: integers or bits to points on the unit circle, and back.
body: The integer at position p (Gray coded from the integer unless `symOrder` is `'bin'`) becomes exp(1i (2 pi p/M + phaseoffset)). `pskdemod` gives the integer (or bits) whose point is nearest in phase.
syntax: With a phase offset and order; from bits.

examples.title: QPSK at pi/4, and 8-PSK's errors at 12 dB

pages.summary: Pulse amplitude modulation: integers or bits to real levels, and back.
body: The levels are -(M-1), -(M-3), ..., M-1, Gray coded unless `'bin'`, turned by a phase offset if given. `pamdemod` gives the integer (or bits) of the nearest level.

pages.summary: Integers as bits and bits as integers.
body: `int2bit` writes each integer as n bits down its column (a column of n bits for each element), the most significant first unless `msbfirst` is false; `bit2int` reads each n bits back. `de2bi` and `bi2de` are the older forms, a row of digits for each number (base 2 unless given), the least significant digit first unless `'left-msb'`.
syntax: Each n bits as an integer.
A row of digits for each number.

pages.summary: Integers as Gray-coded labels of a modulation's points, and back.
body: For `'pam'`, `'psk'` and `'fsk'` the binary-reflected Gray code, in which neighbours differ in one bit; for `'qam'` each axis's half of the bits coded apart, so that neighbours in the grid differ in one bit. The second output is the mapping, the Gray label of each integer.

pages.summary: Bit errors and symbol errors between two sets of integers.
body: `biterr` counts the bits that differ (k bits to each value, as many as the largest needs unless given), with the rate and each element's count; `symerr` counts the elements that differ, with the rate and where they are.

examples.title: One symbol, two bits

pages.summary: Bit and symbol error rates of modulations in white Gaussian noise, worked out exactly.
body: Eb/N0 in dB, the energy per bit over the noise's density; Gray coding. PSK, PAM and square QAM are exact (QAM as two PAMs; PSK from the density of the received phase); differential PSK, FSK and MSK too. A simulation's error rate approaches these as its symbols grow many.

examples.title: Error rates against Eb/N0
examples.code:
EbNo = 0:12;
semilogy(EbNo, berawgn(EbNo, 'psk', 2, 'nondiff'), EbNo, berawgn(EbNo, 'psk', 8, 'nondiff'), EbNo, berawgn(EbNo, 'qam', 16), EbNo, berawgn(EbNo, 'qam', 64))
legend('BPSK', '8-PSK', '16-QAM', '64-QAM', 'Location', 'southwest'), grid on
xlabel('E_b/N_0 (dB)'), ylabel('bit error rate'), ylim([1e-7 1])
berawgn(10, 'psk', 2, 'nondiff')

pages.summary: A raised-cosine filter, to shape symbols into pulses that do not disturb each other.
body: The filter spans `span` symbols at `sps` samples each (span sps + 1 taps), with roll-off beta (0 to 1, the excess bandwidth); `'sqrt'` (the default) is the root raised cosine, used at both ends so that together they make a raised cosine, and `'normal'` the raised cosine itself, which is zero at every other symbol's time. The taps have unit energy.

examples.title: A raised cosine, zero at the other symbols' times
examples.code:
b = rcosdesign(0.35, 6, 8, 'normal');
numel(b)
stem(-24:24, b), xlabel('samples (8 a symbol)')
round(b(1:8:end), 6)

pages.summary: An eye diagram, and a constellation diagram.
body: `eyediagram` draws the signal in traces of n + 1 samples (two symbol periods at n samples a symbol) laid over each other, so that the eye's opening shows how well the symbols can be told apart; a complex signal draws its in-phase and quadrature parts apart. `scatterplot` draws every n-th sample (from offset) as a point, quadrature against in-phase.
syntax: Traces of n samples a symbol.
Every n-th sample, drawn as plotstring says.

examples.title: Pulses shaped and their eye
examples.intro: Root raised cosines at both ends make a raised cosine: at the symbol times the eye is open.
